metadata.title: Wedge's Trial
metadata.description: Logic puzzle game inspired by Gothic Remake's lockpicking mechanics.

footer.disclaimer: This fan-made project is created solely for non-commercial purposes and draws inspiration from the Gothic series. It has no official connection to THQ Nordic or Piranha Bytes, who hold the rights to the Gothic franchise.

hero.title: Every lock hides another test.
hero.lead: Face Wedge’s ever-changing chain of chests, chase a richer haul of ore nuggets, and see how long your nerve—and your lockpicks—hold.
hero.imageAlt: Wedge, the keeper of the trial
hero.quote: A lock tells you everything—if you have the patience to listen.

features.title: A new lock behind every lid
features.lead: No two runs tell quite the same story. Each opened chest leads deeper into an endless trial, where sharper puzzles and a growing ore haul turn every success into an invitation to continue.

items.title: An endless descent
items.body: There is always another chest—and every one raises the stakes.

items.title: Locks that think back
items.body: Interlocking mechanisms make each challenge feel deliberate, readable, and distinct.

items.title: Ore worth the risk
items.body: Build your haul chest by chest and leave a score worthy of the Colony.

origin.title: Why Wedge’s Trial exists
origin.body: Wedge’s Trial began as a personal attempt to turn the lockpicking mechanism from Gothic Remake into a focused browser minigame.

about.title: About Wedge's Trial
about.lead: Wedge’s Trial is an endless browser lockpicking puzzle with gradually growing challenges.

whatItIs.title: What is Wedge’s Trial?
whatItIs.body: Wedge challenges you with a chain of generated, always-solvable locks. Their connected mechanisms reward observation and planning rather than speed, while ore nuggets record how far your run has carried you.

trial.title: The endless trial
trial.body: The first locks introduce a connected pair of plates. As you progress, larger connected groups and longer solutions add to the challenge gradually. Gather as much ore as possible before your lockpicks run out.

inspiration.title: Why it exists
inspiration.body: The project began as a personal attempt to turn the lockpicking mechanism from Gothic Remake into a focused browser minigame.
inspiration.influenceSuffix: , a fan-made lockpicking minigame inspired by Gothic Classic. Wedge’s Trial is a tribute to both ideas and to the creativity of the Gothic community.

howToPlay.title: How to play
howToPlay.lead: Slide the plates left or right until each stationary pin aligns with the middle hole of its plate.

objective.title: Your objective
objective.body: Open each chest, collect its ore nuggets and occasional lockpicks, then face the next, harder lock. The run ends when no lockpicks remain.

mechanism.title: Plates and pins
mechanism.body: Each plate has seven holes and seven permitted positions beneath a stationary pin. Select a plate and slide it left or right. Plate dependencies can also slide connected plates, sometimes in the opposite direction, so watch the whole lock before committing.

steps: Select a plate by clicking or tapping it.
Slide it left or right with the visible controls, A/D, or the Left/Right Arrow keys.
Watch how the selected plate and connected plates slide beneath their stationary pins.
Align the middle hole of every plate with its pin to open the chest.
Claim the reward and continue to the next, harder lock.
rules: A move is invalid if it would push any affected plate outside its permitted position range.
An invalid move changes no plate positions and damages the current lockpick.
A lockpick breaks after exactly 4 invalid moves.
A broken lockpick does not reset the lock or its plate positions.
Manual reset restores the current lock’s starting layout.
When the last lockpick breaks, the run ends.
controls: Click or tap: select a plate
W / Up Arrow and S / Down Arrow: select the previous or next plate
A / Left Arrow and D / Right Arrow: slide the selected plate
N: continue after opening a chest
Visible controls provide the same actions on desktop and mobile.

solver.title: Solver
solver.lead: The generator mixes each lock from a solved state, so every chest stays solvable by construction.
solver.body: That same deterministic model powers the solver and the debug harness used to inspect dependencies, verify solutions, and test invalid-move behavior.
